title.narrative: Action Plan on GBV at the Workplace

description.narrative: Existence of Action Plan and steps for implementation

comment.narrative: The JNCW published the 2020 National Strategy for Women in Jordan 20202025 which makes specific mention of the gaps and proposed legislative amendments that more inclusively tackles the issue GBV in professional environments. The document has now been endorsed and put into effect.

A first draft of the Action Plan is finalised published and presented to the public as well as highlevel political stakeholders at the projects final conference. Further steps for its implementation are outlined and agreed upon in the sustainability workshop before the final conference.

title.narrative: Capacity Building of CBOs/CSOs

description.narrative: Increase in subject knowledge amongst the participants

comment.narrative: Capacity building training sessions will be help to increase competency among CBOsCSOs regarding gender issues and how to handle advocacy campaigns.
At least 80 of training participants show increased knowledge pretraining test and posttraining test

The assessment was carried out using the analytical descriptive approach chosen for its alignment with the projects nature. Data was collected from the sample through a questionnaire. The participants were drawn from three regions of Jordan north south and central.The work team organized workshops in Aqaba Irbid and Zarqa governorates in Jordan. The sessions included pre and postassessments to understand the participants perspectives on genderbased violence in the workplace. Analyzed the assessment results using Microsoft Excel. The final change in knowledge is 85

title.narrative: Community Focus Group Sessions

description.narrative: Attitude of women, family and community members towards female employment and GBV

comment.narrative: Focus community group discussions would contribute towards building trust and awareness campaigns towards GBV. By involving all partners there is a larger contribution towards training and awareness campaigns which will be sustainable and target a larger segment of the local community including those less fortunate and in remote areas. In addition a high consideration should be paid to trustbuilding activities to ensure effectiveness and sustainability.

At least 80 of participants at the community focus group sessions show a shift in attitude towards female employment and have increased awareness of what constitutes GBV presession and postsession surveys
Pre and postassessment results show that 57.3 of the community focus group session participants showed a shift in attitude and increased awareness of GBV.

The Awareness Raising Workshops targeted 30 executive figures and employees from both the private and the public sector in the three selected governorates of Aqaba Irbid and Zarqa. title.narrative: Eliminating GBV in the Workplace in Jordan t media outlets es

description.narrative: To contribute to tackling GBV in Jordan through a strengthened civil society and an improved legal and structural framework for womens employment conditions and labour market participation.ditional businesses. and 3 Women led CSO.

title.narrative: Number of joint statements and actions with CSOs/CBOs on GBV

description.narrative: Joint statements/actions of CSOs/CBOs and other stakeholders on GBV

comment.narrative: 4 of the respondent CSOs from Irbid Zarqa and Aqaba are jointly participating in nationalinternational coalition and network actions that tackle issues of GBV while 20 respondent CSOs from the other governorates are participating in such joint actions. However none of the respondents were recorded in the baseline as having participated in specific joint statements of actions relating to GBV in the workplace.

At least 6 joint public statements events policy papers articles on gender rights and GBV are in the public domain. The disaggregation of the joint statements and actions is fluid and subject to change.

The second year of the project witnessed several joint agreements and statements between several actors the most important of which are three agreements between CSOs announced in Irbid 22. 24. October 2022 Zarqa 01. 03. October 2022 and Aqaba 10.12. September 2022 to provide a support system for victims of GBV at the workplace. The idea of the system was introduced during the dialogue sessions in rural areas. The session facilitators who were affiliated with local CSOs were able to convince women participants of the need to contact them in the case of any kind of violence in order to provide the necessary legal assistance. Another two joint agreements were announced during the implementation of the Awareness Raising Workshops in Irbid 29. March 2023 and Aqaba 26. 27. March 2023. In Irbid the head of the Irbid Governorate Council agreed to work directly with the We Rise Center for Sustainable Development as a representative of CSOs in the governorate in order to strengthen the complaints system in the public and private sectors in the event that women are subject to any form of violence. In Aqaba the employers and executive figures from three private sector companies made a verbal agreement with the Labor Directorate to amend the regulation systems in the private sector in addition to the oversight and monitoring procedures. The CSO Shabab AlGhad Center will follow up with the private sector companies and the Labor Directorate to monitor this agreements implementation.
